s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin, joint, and lung involvement, with a prolonged course of symptoms and significant weight loss
salient_findings: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints with ulcers
Dyspigmentation and atrophy of distal fingers
Interstitial lung disease on chest CT
key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and weight loss
Previous hospitalization for hypoxia
Prior treatment with prednisone
Symmetric joint swelling preventing fist formation
Normal capillaroscopy
Ulcerated lichenoid papules on palmar IP creases
Oxford Scale muscle strength 5 of 5 throughout
Bibasilar rales on auscultation
Elevated ferritin levels (1543 ng/mL)
Depressed creatine kinase levels (32 U/L)
Normal aldolase levels (4.5 U/L)
Lymphocytopenia with CD3: 328 μL, CD4: 233 μL, CD8: 85 μL
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies
Positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies (19.5 units)
Negative results for HIV, anti-Scl-70 antibodies, anti-β2-glycoprotein 1 antibodies, lupus anticoagulant, cryoglobulins, anti-Mi-2 antibodies
Normal prothrombin time, partial thromboplastin time, tissue thromboplastin

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, lymphocytopenia, and multisystem involvement

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of systemic lupus erythematosus, scleroderma, and rheumatoid arthritis features, with interstitial lung disease

shortlist.label: Dermatomyositis
shortlist.why_kept: Skin involvement with ulcerated lichenoid papules, and muscle strength preserved

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and potential lung involvement

shortlist.label: Scleroderma
shortlist.why_kept: Skin thickening and interstitial lung disease, although capillaroscopy was normal

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of symmetric joint swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and skin biopsy findings of orthokeratosis with rare lymphocytes at dermal/epidermal junction and diffuse vasculopathy are consistent with dermatomyositis. Additionally, the patient's muscle strength is normal (Oxford Scale 5 of 5), which is not typical for other myopathies, and the presence of ulcerated lichenoid papules on palmar IP creases (Gottron's papules) is a hallmark of dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies, the overall clinical presentation and lack of other specific lupus criteria make SLE less likely.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not meet the criteria for MCTD, which typically includes a combination of features from lupus, scleroderma, and polymyositis/dermatomyositis.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory findings do not support a diagnosis of Sjögren's syndrome, which primarily affects the exocrine glands.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy and clinical presentation do not show the characteristic sclerotic changes and fibrosis seen in scleroderma.
